chapter: Brawls, the Ink Spots and boyhood recollections
title: Voices in the trio and the later Ink Spots taking the name
summary: Bubbles was tenor, Buck baritone and Sugar Babe soprano; the later famous Ink Spots took the name which could not be copyrighted.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: What was
Tenor singer.
So you two just did harmony with one another.
All three of us. Buck and I only did a duo. No, he wasn't a tenor, he was a baritone -- baritone or a soprano -- Sugar Babe was. I had the tenor voice and Buck had the baritone voice.
Were there other singing groups like that at that time that you had heard that you tried to pattern a bit?
No -uh-uh.
You just came up with the idea of having a --
That's right, that's right, that's exactly right.
Did they ever record the Ink Spots?
No, we didn't make no recording. We didn't but they did.
There is something that exists then.
Yeah, but not of Buck and Sugar Babe and myself, nothing as to that but what I'm telling ya.
Well, when you went off with Buck and Bubbles and the other Ink Spots, how was it taken over by another group?
Well, he was from Indianapolis and he could just use the name because you can't copyright the name, we couldn't copyright that name, at least we didn't.
How long were you together.
Oh, about six weeks. Six weeks as Inks, that's all.
Did the subsequent Ink Spots sing in a similar style as you?
They were different altogether, they were grown people
singing? We were kids singing.
But the name was --

The name is what they had. They had a big reputation. The Ink Spots? I know you've heard of them. So that's what they made out of that. But they weren't the beginners of it. We were the beginners of it, you know.
